forTheMerger.rule: Read the run, not the lane. Every shape below is a way a lane's name misleads, and the run id settles all of them.

forTheRetro.theParentLesson: A derived pin is worth more than a correct constant, and it holds one level up as well: the value you assert in a review must be re-derived from the file at the head, because a citation inside a subagent's finding is a claim rather than a reading. Both of this issue's documentation failures were a single asserted value inside an argument that was otherwise sound, and in both the contradicting evidence was already in the session that asserted it.
forTheRetro.theSharperForm: The architect's generalisation, which I would put above mine: writing to strengthen an argument rather than to describe a system. Neither failure was careless in the ordinary sense; both made the case better, which is why neither was checked. The sentence that makes the argument stronger is the one to re-derive first.
forTheRetro.theSystemProperty: Both failures were claims about a production system neither role can read. A claim about production in operator-facing documentation, written by roles with no production read, should name what it rests on.
forTheRetro.theNarrowingThatMatters: The rule is about the value, not the source. The thermonuclear pair found this issue's two most useful items and an agent found my own stale body line; an entry that said 'do not trust agent findings' would have cost more than both errors. Carry the lead, re-derive the clause.
forTheRetro.theGraceZeroFlinch: When the measured grace was zero I wanted to call it a margin and did not, and the round that followed found the race. A number that makes a design look safe is the one to measure twice.
forTheRetro.myOwnPattern: Three stale lines of mine reached the PR body, one crossing a round boundary with nobody acting, because I wrote each entry when I filed the finding and never read it again — it aged exactly one round behind the document every time. Reading the body at the head is now part of the round, beside reading CI.
